sections.heading: BECOMING GERONIMO
sections.content:
Q: How can I become a woman like Miss Geronimo (Uegoro Natsuki)? I really admire Miss Geronimo!

A: Walk the Superman Road…[ref:kinnikuman-geronimo] no, wait — becoming a police detective is probably the fastest shortcut.

sections.heading: GUNS, GLORY, AND WHICH CHARACTER'S MOST LIKE HIM
sections.content:
Q: Congratulations on the release of Six Guns, Six People, Six Days 1/2! (Note: as written — the correct title is "2/6.") If Iruma-sensei got hold of a handgun, what would you do? Also, which character in Six Guns, Six People, Six Days is most like you?

A: Hand it over to the police, obviously, or so on and so forth. And there's no character in the book who's actually like me — though there is one who shares a certain... preference of mine. I'll keep it a secret which one.

sections.heading: BLUE, WHITE, AND THE COLORLESS CRY OF THE SOUL
sections.content:
Q: What's your favorite color?

A: My favorite is blue, then white, and finally the colorless cry of the soul, pitch-black green… wait, that's not right.[ref:ffu-chant]

sections.heading: A SNACKING SOUND EFFECT
sections.content:
Q: Do you like snacks?

A: Nom nom nom (probably an onomatopoeia for eating).

sections.heading: A COMBAT STORY HE'S IMAGINED
sections.content:
Q: If you were to write a combat-focused story, how would the protagonist fight?

A: I once came up with an idea for a story where the protagonist fights using "the power to turn anything he kills or destroys invisible" — changing the world with it while gradually breaking down in the process, something like that.

sections.heading: BECOMING HIS ILLUSTRATOR
sections.content:
Q: My goal is to become an illustrator. If I manage to go pro, I'd love to illustrate one of Iruma-sensei's works. But it's probably hard for an illustrator to request a specific job like that themselves, isn't it…?

A: I really haven't heard of that sort of thing happening much. That said, I've worked with people who used one of my own works as the subject of their Dengeki Illustration Award submission, so that route seems doable?[ref:dengeki-illust-award]

sections.heading: WAITING ON A CHARACTER WHO WAS NEVER THE LEAD
sections.content:
Q: When will the real heroine of Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy, Hoshinaka Konomi, show up again? I want to read Iruma-sensei's take on Hoshinaka Konomi so badly!

A: Electric Girl is already finished. Besides, if she were really the heroine, the title probably wouldn't be Electric Girl in the first place.

sections.heading: THE LIZARD KING'S SUPERPOWERS, AND ITS STALLED SEQUEL
sections.content:
Q: I love The Lizard King so much — when's the sequel coming out? Also, how do you come up with all those superpowers?

A: When I create them, I keep the powers within a range I can actually describe well. It'd be great if I could properly write that kind of incomprehensible power, but I basically can't, so it ends up losing persuasiveness. As for the sequel, honestly, with everything going on, I can't promise it'll be out this month, so please hold on a little longer (Note: it still hadn't come out by the time of writing).

sections.heading: HOW ELLIO DRESSES FOR WINTER
sections.content:
Q: What does Ellio wear in winter? Her skirt leaves a strong impression, but I don't recall her ever dressing warmly.

A: She wraps herself up in two layers of blanket. Come to think of it, the original story wrapped up during a fairly warm season too.

sections.heading: WHY THAT PARTICULAR DAY
sections.content:
Q: Liar, Broken has a lot of characters who are, good or bad, fairly "that way" — did you research mental-health material while writing them and her? Also, Akkyun had already had contact with Ma-chan before, but he chose that particular day to "reconnect" — was there a specific reason for that? Reading it, I kept thinking, he'd had chances to reach out all along…

A: I didn't do any special research. If I had, the writing would've gotten more clinical and technical, and the story might've drifted off track. As for why he chose that day — it's because the story of Volume 1 begins on that day. That might sound a little meta, but really, everything about all of us begins on the day we were born too. So, that is, um, that's basically it.

sections.heading: IS FAN WORK OKAY?
sections.content:
Q: Iruma Hitoma-sensei, is it okay for everyone to make derivative fan works of your stories?

A: Personally, it's completely fine by me. But there's a lot of grown-up business involved, so I can't publicly say "go wild, have at it!"

sections.heading: WHAT HAPPENED TO KAZUKI?
sections.content:
Q: I'm curious what happens to Kazuki (Nagase Kazuki, Nagase Tooru's little sister) after Volumes 9 and 10 of Liar, Broken — will she show up again in any future cameos?

A: Hmm — how would that go, I honestly don't know (I can't say I've forgotten, exactly).

sections.heading: A BOOK FOR OOE YUNA?
sections.content:
Q: I love Ooe Yuna so much I can't focus in class anymore. That's bad! Won't you write a book with Ooe Yuna as the lead? (^^;

A: Same answer as the last question — it's been so long now that I think writing her again would just feel off. I don't think I could actually live up to everyone's expectations there.

sections.heading: VOLUME 3 IN AUGUST
sections.content:
Q: Iruma-sensei, here's my question. Will Adachi and Shimamura get a third volume?

A: August, probably.

sections.heading: SEQUEL PLANS, OR THE LACK THEREOF
sections.content:
Q: Any plans for a sequel to Adachi and Shimamura or Tamako and the Yellow Chicken? It'd be great if there were!

A: Nothing planned for Tamako right now, but Adachi and Shimamura will get one.

sections.heading: RATING THE CAST'S LOOKS
sections.content:
Q: I tried rating your characters' handsome-guy scores! First, I feel like Akkyun doesn't quite fit the word "handsome," so 40 IP (Ikemen Points). Tokage-kun, being drawn by Buriki, obviously earns 70 IP (+10 IP if he's got bandages on), and Midorikawa scores even higher once his hair turns white. Niwa-kun's face is a bit girlish so he's a bit lower, 60 IP. The two leads of The Naked Idiot get 50 IP for their "chasing-my-dreams" vibe. Kisogawa-kun scores surprisingly high, 85 IP (I think there's some kind of protagonist-adjacent handsome-bonus going on). So — how many Ikemen Points does Iruma-sensei have? By the way, like Elliott, my own detector is broken, so I can't measure it myself.

A: Probably about the same as the combat power of the first person Raditz ran into.[ref:dragonball-raditz]

sections.heading: WHAT KISOGAWA DOES ON HIS DAYS OFF
sections.content:
Q: I wanted to fill an entire shelf with Iruma-sensei's books, so I bought a Color Box (a small storage cabinet). By the way, I wanted to ask — what does Kisogawa do when he's not working?

A: Maybe he goes back to his hometown to eat a home-cooked meal or something. I just thought of that on the spot.

sections.heading: TOO DISTRACTED TO STUDY
sections.content:
Q: I love Iruma-sensei's work so much that I can't focus on studying anymore. What should I do?

A: Then rewire your brain so you don't need to study anymore. Not possible? No, it's not. Alright, open the book and start studying.

sections.heading: A FAVORITE MUSICIAN
sections.content:
Q: Does Iruma-sensei like "Os-Uchūjin," the opening theme for Electric Girl? Also, do you have a favorite musician or performer?

A: I like Taro Hakase.[ref:taro-hakase] He counts as a performer too, right? Doesn't he?

sections.heading: WHICH PUBLISHER WOULD I FIND YOU AT?
sections.content:
Q: I want to become a novelist! Or rather, I've written some novel-like things purely as a hobby. Since that's the extent of my mental preparation, I don't know much about the novelist profession or the industry (though I know a few publisher-imprint names). Is there an imprint where "if you work here, you can meet me"?

A: Funny, I don't know much about this industry either. It's probably Dengeki Bunko, though.

sections.heading: A VALENTINE'S STORY IN THE DEAD OF SUMMER
sections.content:
Q: Adachi and Shimamura is a lot of fun — will there be a third volume? Adachi's virgin energy is exploding in my brain.

A: Scheduled for an August release. Even though it'll be the height of summer, the book is actually a Valentine's Day story. The chocolate might melt. Also, I'm still trying to figure out the surnames of the main characters going forward — somebody help me think of some.

sections.heading: REVENGE VIA FLYING KNEE KICK
sections.content:
Q: Question: I want to hit a friend who just got married in the head with a flying knee kick. How should I go about it?

A: Go read Kick no Oni and practice — that manga is, in fact, said to be based on a true story.[ref:kick-no-oni]

sections.heading: WRITING FOR OTHER PUBLISHERS
sections.content:
Q: Would you publish with a light-novel imprint or publisher other than Dengeki Bunko or MediaWorks Bunko?

A: If someone came and offered me the work, I'd want to do it. Though nobody's going to. But if my reputation grows enough that people feel it'd be a waste to leave me alone, someone will probably come find me eventually. I believe I've added something of real value to the world, so I'll just wait patiently.

sections.heading: ON CHANGING WRITING STYLES
sections.content:
Q: I've bought pretty much everything Iruma-sensei has written! I feel like Liar, Broken, The Lizard King, and Electric Girl all have somewhat different writing styles — was that a deliberate stylistic shift, or did it happen unconsciously? Personally, I prefer the style of Liar, Broken. Also, do you have any plans to write another protagonist like Edase Akkyun? I love Edase Akkyun the most!

A: Thank you for buying almost everything. But when you say a character "like him" — what kind of character do you mean? I think he's pretty ordinary, honestly. Also, rereading it now, I don't actually like my own writing style from the Liar, Broken era, because my prose was pretty rough back then.

sections.heading: NO SINGLE FAVORITE CHARACTER
sections.content:
Q: Among the characters in your own work, who's Iruma-sensei's favorite?

A: I don't really have a single favorite. I tend to like pretty much any character with a rotten personality.

sections.heading: STILL NO SEASON 2
sections.content:
Q: Will Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy get a second season?

A: The production staff seem pretty busy, so…

sections.heading: A DROPPED CONTINUITY THREAD
sections.content:
Q: Be honest — is Amano Misa the same person as Hoshimimi?

A: There was originally a plan for that, but a mistake in the timeline math meant that idea had to be scrapped.[ref:amano-misa-hoshimimi]

sections.heading: PITCHING THE NEW RELEASES
sections.content:
Q: New books are about to come out~! I'm really looking forward to both Europa (Note: From the Bottom of Europa) and Fuwafuwa (Note: The Fluffy Girl Falls from the Sky), but I want to hear Iruma-sensei personally hype up what's fun about them!!

A: Oh, sure. Fuwafuwa is a romantic comedy about a twisted jerk of a protagonist panting "h-huh… huh…" over his older sister, who's ten years his senior (slightly exaggerated). And Europa is… ah, by the way, this question came from a Mr. Kazuma Miki, living in Tokyo — thanks for writing in![ref:miki-kazuma] …Hey, wait, haven't you read the manuscript? Wouldn't you already know all this if you'd actually read it? Isn't this just supposed to be a plain promotional plug? Anyway, that's the gist of the story.

references.title: Geronimo and the "Superman Road"
references.note: Geronimo is a character from the manga/anime Kinnikuman who was once a human before undergoing the trial known as the "Superman Road" (Sūpāman Rōdo) to be reborn as a true chōjin ("superman"). Iruma jokingly starts to suggest this fictional trial as the path to becoming admirable before catching himself and giving a more down-to-earth answer.

references.title: The FF:U Color Incantation
references.note: Iruma is quoting (loosely) a stylized, color-themed battle incantation associated with the protagonist of FF:U ~Final Fantasy: Unlimited~, a GONZO-produced anime that aired from October 2001 to March 2002, tied into Square's Final Fantasy brand as an original, non-game spin-off story.

references.title: The Dengeki Illustration Award
references.note: Entrants to the Dengeki Illustration Award must submit illustrations based on an existing Dengeki Bunko or MediaWorks Bunko work; award-winning interviews describe successful applicants choosing a specific series — such as Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy — as their submission's subject. Winners occasionally go on to collaborate directly with the original author through official tie-in projects, which is the route Iruma is referring to here.

references.title: Raditz's Scouter Joke
references.note: In Dragon Ball, the invading Saiyan Raditz famously scoffs at Earth's strongest fighter after his scouter reads a laughably low "combat power of 5." Iruma self-deprecatingly compares his own hypothetical Ikemen Score to that number.

references.title: Taro Hakase
references.note: Taro Hakase is a well-known Japanese violinist and composer, popular for blending classical violin with pop and jazz influences.

references.title: Kick no Oni and Tadashi Sawamura
references.note: Kick no Oni ("The Demon of Kicking") is a manga by Ikki Kajiwara dramatizing the career of real-life kickboxer Tadashi Sawamura, whose signature move was the "vacuum flying knee kick" — a genuine technique from his actual fighting career, which the manga fictionalizes but roots in real events.

references.title: Amano Misa and Hoshimimi
references.note: Amano Misa is the biological mother of Amano ×, the protagonist of Liar, Broken, killed by her husband at age 32. Hoshimimi is a childhood friend of Fujiwa Jojo and Elliott in Electric Girl and Adolescent Boy, the same age as Jojo, who once turned down a confession from Elliott, became pregnant and dropped out of high school as a teenager, and had already died years before the story's present day. The two characters share small details (such as a fondness for tearing up books), and Iruma had originally intended them to be the same person — but an inconsistency in their respective ages made that impossible, so the idea was abandoned.

references.title: Kazuma Miki
references.note: Kazuma Miki was Iruma Hitoma's first editor at Dengeki Bunko and has been credited as an editor on other notable light novel series as well. Iruma's aside jokingly "outs" this question as having come from his own editor rather than an ordinary reader.
